page.layout: One printed page, the right-hand page of the opening. Running head at the top centre, page number at the top right. The text block is one column of full-width text with italic passages and a numbered canon. No marginal notes on this page. The left-hand strip is the edge of the facing page and is not transcribed.

main_text.p: Officium subditorum religiosum inter sese, habet hunc Canonem:

p.i: Subditi sibi mutuo praestent officia non tantum coniunctionis Ethicae & Politicae, sed etiam coniunctionis Christianae & dilectionis fraternae: Peregrinos quoq; exteros secum habitantes Christianâ patientia & hospitalitate ferant, iuvent, & foveant.
Et sic de statu religioso pacato: Sequitur status Religiosus affectus, sive turbatus; qui duplex est, nempe vel leuiter turbatus, vel grauiter.

main_text.p: Leuiter turbatus status religiosus est, vel ob nudū dissensum principis à subditorum religione, vel ob dissensum subditorum à religione principis, vel ob dissensū religionis inter ipsos subditos. de quo statu sunt hi Canones:

I Princeps qui veram religionem profitetur, perfectior est eo, qui à religione est alienus: interim tamen is qui alienus est à vera religione, propterea, quia alienus est, non definit esse legitimus princeps, multo minus debet haberi pro tyranno, aut pro tali, cui iure subditi se possint opponere.

Nimirū princeps, qui à religione dissentit, & interim tamen subditos suos ad ciuile bonum ducit ac dirigit, retinet adhuc fundamenta principatus, ea nempe, quae pertinent ad statum Politicum absolute consideratum, & idcirco obedientia etiam ei & honor debetur. Euangeliū enim & religio Christiana non tollit honestatem, neque Politias[?] ad bonum ciuile, & ad honestatem compositę ad pietatem, etiamsi non sunt compositę ad pietatem,

page.notes: The text ends mid-sentence at the foot of the page; the last line reads "Politias" (possibly "Politicas") and the line "compositę ad pietatem" is printed as shown, with the phrase repeated at the line end. Lines are copied from the scan; the left-hand facing page is cut off and not transcribed. The canon number "I" is a paragraph opener, not a heading.
